title: Noninvasive quantitative MRI of pulmonary perfusion using pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling (PCASL): Method development of a multiple-labeling approach and clinical application
summary:
Persistent breathing difficulties and shortness of breath are a common clinical problem both following acute pulmonary embolism and in chronic lung diseases, and are associated with reduced physical performance and quality of life. This is often due to impaired blood flow to the lungs. Established imaging techniques are available in routine clinical practice for assessing so-called pulmonary perfusion (lung blood flow), particularly ventilation-perfusion scintigraphy and contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT).  Both methods have high diagnostic value and are firmly established in clinical diagnostics. In certain clinical situations, however—such as during repeated follow-up examinations or in younger patients—there may be a need for supplementary radiation-free imaging modalities.
Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) offers the possibility of radiation-free functional lung imaging. In particular, MRI-based perfusion imaging using so-called arterial spin labeling (ASL) allows for the visualization of regional pulmonary perfusion without the administration of contrast agents. This method could therefore provide additional information on pulmonary perfusion and is generally suitable for repeated examinations as part of follow-up observations. 
This study evaluates the diagnostic accuracy of ASL MRI in various patient populations and compares it with the respective standard diagnostic methods.
conditions: Substudy 1: Healthy subjects; Substudy 2: Patients indicated for pulmonary perfusion scintigraphy; Substudy 3: Patients with a clinical indication for follow-up after LAE and evidence of thrombi on CTPA; Substudy 4: Patients with cystic fibrosis, including adolescents

interventions.name: Arm 1 (Cohort 1): Healthy subjects undergoing ASL MRI (2 scans) of the lungs on a 1.5T scanner.

Arm 2 (Cohorts 2–4): Patients undergoing ASL MRI (1 scan) of the lungs. 
For the patients, the clinically indicated diagnostic procedures are used as intra-individual comparisons (Cohort 2: lung perfusion scintigraphy; Cohort 3: CTPA, echocardiography; Cohort 4: MRI, spirometry).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Cohort 1: 
• Healthy volunteers
• Consent to be notified of incidental findings
Cohort 2: 
• Clinical indication for pulmonary perfusion scintigraphy
Cohort 3: 
• Clinical indication for follow-up after acute pulmonary embolism (APE) and detection of thrombi on CTPA
• Hemodynamically stable patients
• No intensive care required
Cohort 4: 
• Patients diagnosed with cystic fibrosis
• Children, adolescents, and adults (generally ages 5 and up)
• Clinical indication for routine MRI without anesthesia
Exclusion criteria:
Cohorts 1–4
• Pregnant or breastfeeding women
• General contraindications for an MRI scan
• Need for anesthesia to perform an MRI
• No written consent from the subject, patient, or legal guardian
• Cohort 1 only: Smokers, acute or chronic lung disease
